where: Section 1, first formula and symbol list
problem: The total-pressure equation P = pA + pB uses pB and xB, but the symbol list defines only pA, xA, P°A and P. A student meeting pB for the first time has to guess what it means.
fix: Add to the symbol list: pB is the partial pressure of B (kPa); xB is the liquid mole fraction of B, with xB = 1 − xA; P°B is the pure-B vapour pressure at the same temperature (kPa).

where: Section 1, last paragraph and exam trap 4
problem: The statement that a two-phase mixture needs P between P°B and P°A is only a necessary condition. A mixture whose overall composition is rich in A can already be all liquid at a pressure below P°A. A student may read 'between P°B and P°A' as meaning 'then it is two-phase'.
fix: Say it as a one-way test: for any two-phase mixture at a fixed temperature, P must lie between P°B and P°A; but P inside that range does not by itself guarantee two phases — the overall composition decides that. Also state that these pressure rules hold at a fixed temperature, since P°A and P°B change with temperature.

problem: 'Some syllabi call this vapour-liquid equilibrium (VLE)' reads oddly, because the paragraph is already describing VLE, not a special case of it.
fix: Write: 'This balance between a liquid and its vapour is called vapour-liquid equilibrium (VLE).'
